summary.headline: Texmaco Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose about 15% QoQ to INR863 crore, but was down sharply YoY on weaker Indian Railway wagon orders.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR863 crore (about INR860 crore per the CFO), up roughly 15% QoQ from INR753 crore but about INR386 crore lower than the roughly INR1,250 crore of Q2 FY26, mainly in freight cars. EBITDA was about INR88 crore at a 10.2% margin versus 10.8% in Q1, and PBT was INR51 crore (5.9% margin) versus INR44 crore in Q1. Q2 PBT was supported by a one-time JV gain of about INR75-76 crore (per an analyst), and other income fell to INR14.7 crore from INR24.9 crore. Management stressed a shift in mix toward private and export orders, which now make up roughly 80-85% of the order book.

financial_highlights.change: vs 68.8% in Q1 and 74.7% a year ago

segments.name: Freight rolling stock
segments.commentary: Freight cars were 62.3% of standalone turnover in Q2 (68.8% in Q1, 74.7% a year ago). Freight rolling stock order book is about INR8,000 crore, executable over this year and next; about 7,200 wagons pending.

segments.name: Infra rail and electrical
segments.commentary: Rail infra revenue grew about 41-42% QoQ and electrical infra about 38% QoQ. Electrical revenue reached about INR250 crore in the quarter, with an order backlog of about INR1,600 crore executable over this year and the next four quarters.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Produced 6,468 metric tons in Q2. Combined capacity is about 60,000 metric tons; H1 FY27 dispatch guided at 35,000-40,000 metric tons, with 25-30% exports.

segments.name: Other infra and components
segments.commentary: Other infra and component order deliverables of about INR3,000-3,500 crore spanning this year and next. EPC business turned profitable, though only marginally.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share of order book rose to 54% from 9% a year ago. Management says exports carry higher margins. A South Africa order of about INR4,000 crore includes locomotives (about INR1,300 crore) and wagons, with delivery in FY28 plus one quarter and a 15-year maintenance tail.

guidance_outlook: Freight rolling stock order book of about INR8,000 crore executable over FY27 and FY28; management says all rolling stock orders are executable within about 10 quarters.
Management expects results to be better than the prior quarter from Q3 onward, with a stronger rebound in H2 FY27.
Management expects to retain or improve EBITDA margins through cost initiatives, lower finance costs after the rating upgrade, and better mix.
South Africa order revenue to begin in FY28, not in FY27. A South Africa facility will be set up for maintenance.

Capex: about 40% of the year's planned capex executed; no capex planned for the core business; INR200 crore earmarked for defence. Management sees no need for debt in the short term, with debt retiring every quarter.

Texmaco 2.0 target of INR9,000-10,000 crore top line, with a core contribution of INR4,000-5,000 crore and INR5,000-6,000 crore from adjacencies and new businesses (wheels, passenger mobility, defence, renewables). Management said early revenue from new businesses may be too ambitious this year.
capex_capacity: About 40% of the planned FY27 capex has been executed; the exact full-year number is not yet fixed. Capex is directed at growth businesses, not the core.
Foundry capacity is about 60,000 metric tons combined across both foundries, up from 20,000-25,000 metric tons a couple of years ago; management says capacity is not a constraint.
Wheels JV MoU signed; management aims for a broad wheel range covering heavy haul and high-speed trains. Timeline not given.
Nymwag JV in India received initial G-105 certification from RDSO; the plant is described as production-ready, pending a prototype order from Railways.
A South Africa facility will be set up mainly for maintenance; locomotive supply to come from India, with a Make in India locomotive being sought.
demand_pricing: Order book mix: about 80-85% private and export, about 15-16% Indian Railways. The company says Indian Railways was about 1-1.5% of the order book in one analyst's reading of the presentation.

A recent Indian Railways option-clause order of about INR400 crore (wagons for coal transport) was allocated by existing contract history. Management says it cannot give a timeline for further Railways orders.

Management stated export margins are much higher than domestic. An analyst put the export order book at about INR5,800 crore with about INR700 crore of provisions, which management said is a risk-mitigation measure unrelated to future orders.
Private wagon win of about INR426-427 crore was cited by an analyst, with more private and export inflows expected from this month.
Payment risk: management said most export contracts are LC-backed, and a significant share of contract value is advance-paid or milestone-linked, so payment delays are not seen as a material risk.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company manage order delays and custom designs as it shifts to private and export, and keep factories full without relying on government tenders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said diversification is deliberate, targeting no single customer or domain above 40%. Private and export wagons are different types with lower unit volumes than the commodity wagons, and about INR8,000 crore of freight orders are executable over FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Excluding the one-time JV gain, is core profit lower, and how will margins hold if raw material prices rise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said EBITDA was defended via waste reduction, supply-chain cost work, power, fuel and freight initiatives, and lower finance cost after the rating upgrade. He expects to retain or improve margins through mix.

qa_highlights.question: The South Africa order and locomotive scope: who will build the locomotives, and what is the FY28 execution?
qa_highlights.answer: The contract runs to FY28 plus one quarter, with a 15-year maintenance tail. Locomotive manufacturing involvement is under discussion, with supply from India. Management did not name whether a Wabtec JV or standalone entity would supply.

qa_highlights.question: What was the INR700 crore provision on exports, and why did margins look compressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision was a risk-mitigation measure, not linked to specific orders, and will not affect future export returns. It was disclosed in a prior quarter's note, and management did not repeat detail on the call.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and debt profile over the next 2-3 years, and how the INR9,000-10,000 crore Texmaco 2.0 target will be funded.
qa_highlights.answer: About 40% of the planned capex is executed. Debt is declining each quarter and internal accruals should cover growth and maintenance capex. The company will return with more capex detail as businesses take shape; INR200 crore is earmarked for defence.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of the RVNL JV and the Nymwag and foundry outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: RVNL JV is waiting for a sizeable tender, which management expects within this FY. Nymwag plant is production-ready, pending a prototype order. Foundry capacity is not a constraint; H1 dispatch is 35,000-40,000 metric tons with 25-30% export.

risks_watch: Q2 revenue down about 31% YoY on lower Indian Railway orders; recovery depends on H2 execution and new private and export inflows.

Management did not clearly explain the roughly INR700 crore export provision or the non-repeatable items in Q1 and Q2 other income. Analysts pressed for detail, and management deferred to a published note.
Q2 PBT was helped by a one-time JV gain of about INR75-76 crore; core profitability is weaker than last year.
Execution timing of the South Africa order (FY28 onward) and the locomotive sourcing arrangement are still open.
Texmaco 2.0 funding: a sizeable INR9,000-10,000 crore top line target with no clear capex or funding path beyond the INR200 crore defence capex.
Repeated analyst concerns about the company's record of quarterly improvement, and the pace of RVNL JV and Nymwag commercialisation.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on order book, export mix and the Texmaco 2.0 strategy, but evasive on the INR700 crore provision, the timing of Indian Railway orders, and the RVNL JV. Management repeatedly deferred specific numbers to later updates.
key_quotes: And the ratios of the order book today qualitatively changes for Texmaco in terms of the core business.
So we feel that we have a very clear path now, and we don't envisage any obstacle in terms of execution of this.
I think the tipping point has come.
But I cannot just indicate you a time, which I hope you will appreciate.

adds.what: Foundry capacity about 60,000 metric tons combined (not a new addition; existing base, up from 20,000-25,000 t a couple of years ago)
Nymwag JV India plant, production-ready after initial G-105 RDSO certification, pending prototype order from Railways
South Africa maintenance facility (timing not given; revenue from FY28 onward)

growth.why: Management expects better results from Q3 onward with a stronger H2 FY27 rebound and a Texmaco 2.0 target of INR9,000-10,000 crore, backed by an ~INR8,000 crore freight rolling stock order book executable over FY27-FY28 and ~INR1,600 crore electrical backlog, but gave no numeric quarterly guidance and no new capacity timelines.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects to retain or improve EBITDA margin (Q2 at 10.2% vs 10.8% in Q1, ~70 bps higher ex non-repeatable other income) via cost initiatives, lower finance cost after rating upgrade, and export/private mix that management says carries higher margins.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Foundry capacity is already about 60,000 MT and management says it is not a constraint; the only new facility is a South Africa maintenance facility with no timeline, and the Nymwag plant is production-ready but awaiting a prototype order.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: Q3 FY27 onward; stronger H2 FY27
rows.why: Wagon deliveries rose to about 1,106 in Q2 from Q1, revenue up 15% QoQ to INR863 crore, and freight rolling stock order book of about INR8,000 crore is executable over FY27-FY28; however revenue is still down about 31% YoY from about INR1,250 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: About 40% of FY27 capex is executed with the full-year figure not fixed; capex is directed at growth businesses (INR200 crore defence earmarked), but no core-business capex and no new capacity utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is 'very much hopeful' of better results from Q3 onward and a stronger H2 rebound, but gave no numeric guidance; the INR8,000 crore freight order book and INR1,600 crore electrical backlog support it, though Indian Railway orders have no timeline.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 PBT of INR51 crore was helped by a one-time JV gain of about INR75-76 crore, core profit is below last year, Indian Railway order flow has no timeline, and the South Africa revenue only starts in FY28.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wheels JV MoU signed with no timeline, Nymwag G-105 certified and production-ready pending a prototype order, and the South Africa locomotive scope is still under discussion.

rows.label: South Africa order (~INR4,000 cr) revenue from FY28
rows.why: Contract of about INR4,000 crore includes locomotives (about INR1,300 crore) and wagons, with revenue starting next fiscal and a 15-year maintenance tail, so it is firmly committed but has no FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Export mix shift and margin uplift
rows.why: Export share of order book rose to 54% from 9% a year ago and management says exports carry higher margins, though the INR700 crore export provision and the margin drivers were not clearly explained.

rows.label: Debt retiring each quarter
rows.why: Management says debt is retiring every quarter, no debt is needed in the short term, and finance costs fall after the rating upgrade.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, export mix, and the Texmaco 2.0 strategy, but cautious on the timing of Indian Railway orders, and deferred on the INR700 crore export provision, non-repeatable other income and the RVNL JV; analysts pressed on core profit ex the JV gain and the margin def

oneOffs.what: One-time JV gain of about INR75-76 crore in Q2 FY27 PBT (per analyst)
Q1 FY27 other income included non-repeatable items; other income fell to INR14.7 crore from INR24.9 crore
Year-ago Q2 FY26 base of roughly INR1,250 crore revenue, with freight cars at 74.7% of turnover; the YoY decline reflects a high base of Indian Railway wagon orders rather than a one-off gain

quality.why: Revenue was about INR863 crore, up about 15% QoQ but down roughly 31% YoY from about INR1,250 crore on weaker Indian Railway wagon orders, so the QoQ gain comes from execution and mix, not a one-off. Q2 PBT of INR51 crore is flattered by a one-time JV gain of about INR75-76 crore, which exceeds total PBT, so core profit is weaker than the headline.
